title: Smooth pullback of the finite normalization quotient sequence
statement:
Let $S$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $h:T	o S$ be a quasi-compact smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $
u_X:X^
u	o X$ for the componentwise normalization of a scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] and $C_X=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_X	o
u_{X,*}\mathcal O_{X^
u})$ [def-trf-conductor-cokernel]. Then $T$ is reduced and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and there is a canonical isomorphism of $T$-schemes
$$	heta_h:T^
u\xrightarrow{\sim}S^
u	imes_S T,$$
where the map on the right to $T$ is the second projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. With module pullback as in [def-pc-module-pullback], there are canonical isomorphisms
$$\alpha_h:h^*(
u_{S,*}\mathcal O_{S^
u})\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_{T,*}\mathcal O_{T^
u},\qquad  eta_h:h^*C_S\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T.$$
Together with $h^*\mathcal O_S\cong\mathcal O_T$, these identify the pullback of the short exact normalization sequence on $S$ with the short exact normalization sequence on $T$, including its structure-sheaf inclusion and quotient map. Explicitly, for affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T$ with $h(V)\subseteq U$, put $N=\Gamma(
u_S^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_{S^
u})$. The ring map $A	o B$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The isomorphism $\alpha_h$ on $V$ is the finite-algebra comparison $N\otimes_A B\cong\Gamma(
u_T^{-1}(V),\mathcal O_{T^
u})$, and $ eta_h$ is the induced quotient comparison
$$(N/A)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}(N\otimes_A B)/B,$$
where $B$ is embedded by $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. These comparisons restrict compatibly to smaller opens and respect identities and composition under the canonical pullback composition isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 07TD, lemma-normalization-and-smooth; finite-algebra and cokernel comparison is the agent affine deduction detailed in report.md. The retained normalized-blowup route is ILO Expose VIII, 2.2.1--2.2.4 and Lemma 2.2.9, printed pp.90--91 (literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf), specialized to the unit ideal.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and one. Thus S is Noetherian by finite-type permanence. Smoothness makes h flat and locally of finite presentation. A finitely presented algebra is finitely generated, so h is locally of finite type; quasi-compactness makes it finite type. Finite-type composition gives T of finite type over Q, hence Noetherian by the same permanence theorem. Smooth reduced ascent gives reduced T.

Apply reduced algebraic normalization over the field Q to S and T: both componentwise normalization morphisms are finite. The finite-normalization quotient lemma now gives both short exact sequences, and on every affine U=Spec A the finite algebra N and the quotient module N/A representing C_S. The same applies to affine opens of T.

proof.text: The unit ideal O_S is quasi-coherent of finite type (locally it is the free module of rank one), hence coherent on the locally Noetherian S. Its zero scheme is empty. Apply normalized-blowup calculus with J=O_S. Its unit-ideal identification B_{O_S}(S)=S^nu and its smooth comparison give theta_h:T^nu ≅ S^nu ×_S T over T. This also supplies identity and composition compatibility of theta_h, retaining the normalized-blowup route.

source.place: Expose VIII 2.2.1--2.2.4 and Lemma 2.2.9, printed pp.90--91, unit-ideal specialization; coherent.tex Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian).

proof.text: A finite morphism is affine by definition. Apply affine pushforward base change, clause (2), to nu_S and its structure sheaf, and identify the base-changed scheme with T^nu using theta_h. This defines the algebra isomorphism alpha_h. On V=Spec B above U=Spec A it is the finite-algebra comparison N tensor_A B with the normalization algebra on V (switching tensor factors in the cited formula). Since it is a unital B-algebra comparison, it carries 1 tensor b to the image of b. The structure-sheaf pullback isomorphism therefore makes its square with the normalization inclusions commute.

source.place: Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), applied to the structure sheaf, with its affine tensor formula.

proof.text: Flat pullback is exact, so pulling back the short exact sequence from step 2 is short exact. The commuting square from step 4 identifies its first two arrows with those for T; taking cokernels gives the unique isomorphism beta_h commuting with quotient maps. For the affine formula, h is flat, hence A to B is flat by the affine criterion. Affine pullback sections and the quotient lemma identify the pulled-back quotient with (N/A) tensor_A B. Flat tensor exactness and tensor right exactness identify this with (N tensor_A B)/B: explicitly [n] tensor b maps to [n tensor b]. The submodule is exactly the image of A tensor_A B=B, embedded by b mapping to 1 tensor b; flatness ensures this embedding is injective.

source.place: Tag 02N4 (lemma-pullback-flat); morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); schemes.tex Tag 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback); algebra.tex Tags 00HD (lemma-flat) and 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact).

proof.text: The comparisons just constructed are global sheaf maps. Their affine descriptions thus commute with restrictions, and the sheaf-on-a-basis lemma also checks their equality on arbitrary opens. Let h':U'→T be a further quasi-compact smooth morphism. The composite h h' is smooth by smooth composition; h' is of finite type as in step 1 (applied to T), so h h' is of finite type by finite-type composition, in particular quasi-compact, and the item applies to h h'. Then theta agrees with the iterated comparison by normalized-blowup calculus; alpha agrees by clause (3) of affine pushforward base change. In coordinates A to B to D, tensor reassociation sends (n tensor b) tensor c to n tensor (b c), with b acting through B to D; both quotient comparisons send ([n] tensor b) tensor c to [n tensor (b c)]. Equivalently, the two beta maps agree after the epimorphic pulled-back quotient map, hence agree. For the identity the formula is n tensor a mapping to an and its quotient. These are precisely the canonical pullback compositors and prove all asserted identity and composition compatibilities.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_normalization_quotient_comparison (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced S] (q : S ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℚ))) [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [QuasiCompact q] (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ S) [Smooth h] [QuasiCompact h] : IsReduced T ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (h ≫ q) ∧ QuasiCompact (h ≫ q) ∧ IsFinite S.fromReducedNormalization ∧ IsFinite T.fromReducedNormalization ∧ (∃! d : Comparison h, Canonical d) ∧ (∀ d : Comparison (𝟙 S), Canonical d → d.normalizationMap = 𝟙 S.reducedNormalization ∧ d.alpha.hom = (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionId S).hom.app (algebra S) ∧ d.beta.hom = (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionId S).hom.app (conductorCokernel S)) ∧ (∀ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ T) [Smooth g] [QuasiCompact g] (dh : Comparison h) (dg : Comparison g) (dgh : Comparison (g ≫ h)), Canonical dh → Canonical dg → Canonical dgh → dgh.normalizationMap = dg.normalizationMap ≫ dh.normalizationMap ∧ dgh.alpha.hom = (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionComp g h).hom.app (algebra S) ≫ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).map dh.alpha.hom ≫ dg.alpha.hom ∧ dgh.beta.hom = (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackSectionComp g h).hom.app (conductorCokernel S) ≫ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).map dh.beta.hom ≫ dg.beta.hom)
